items.stem: The middle most observation of every data arranged in order is called
items.answer: When all the observations are arranged in ascending or descending order, the observation lying in the middle is the median. Hence the middle most observation is called the median.

items.stem: For some data x₁, x₂, ...............xₙ with respective frequencies f₁, f₂, ......fₙ, the value of Σ₁ⁿ fᵢ(xᵢ − x̄) is equal to
items.answer: Σfᵢ(xᵢ − x̄) = Σfᵢxᵢ − x̄Σfᵢ. Since x̄ = Σfᵢxᵢ / Σfᵢ, we have x̄Σfᵢ = Σfᵢxᵢ, so the difference is 0. Hence Σfᵢ(xᵢ − x̄) = 0.

items.stem: The median and mode respectively of a frequency distribution are 26 and 29, Then its mean is
items.answer: By the empirical relation Mₒ = 3M_d − 2M, with Mₒ = 29 and M_d = 26: 29 = 3 × 26 − 2M, so 2M = 78 − 29 = 49 and M = 49/2 = 24.5. The mean is 24.5.

items.stem: The cumulative frequency table is useful in determining
items.answer: A cumulative frequency table is a running total of the frequencies. From it the mean, the median and the mode of the distribution can all be found, so it is useful in determining all of these.

items.stem: In a frequency distribution, the mid value of a class is 10 and the width of the class is 6. The lower limit of the class is
items.answer: Let x be the upper limit and y the lower limit. The mid value gives (x + y)/2 = 10, i.e. x + y = 20. The width gives x − y = 6. Solving the two equations, y = 7. The lower limit of the class is 7.

items.stem: For finding the popular size of readymade garments, which central tendency is used?
items.answer: The popular size is the size that occurs most often, and the measure of central tendency that picks the most frequent value is the mode. Hence mode is used.

items.stem: If the difference of mode and median of a data is 24, then the difference of median and mean is
items.answer: Given Mₒ − M_d = 24. Using Mₒ = 3M_d − 2M, Mₒ − M_d = 2M_d − 2M = 2(M_d − M). So 24 = 2(M_d − M) and M_d − M = 12. The difference of median and mean is 12.

items.answer: The mode is the value with the highest frequency. Here 8 occurs eight times, more often than 4 (three times), 5 (five), 6 (six) or 10 (seven). Hence the mode is 8.

items.stem: Find the class-marks of the classes 10-25 and 35-55.
items.answer: The class mark is the average of the two class limits. For 10−25 the class mark is (10 + 25)/2 = 35/2 = 17.5, and for 35−55 it is (35 + 55)/2 = 90/2 = 45. Hence the class marks are 17.5 and 45.

items.stem: Prove that Σ(xᵢ − x̄) = 0
items.answer:
By definition the mean is x̄ = (1/n) Σxᵢ, so nx̄ = Σxᵢ.
Now Σ(xᵢ − x̄) = (x₁ − x̄) + (x₂ − x̄) + … + (xₙ − x̄) = (x₁ + x₂ + … + xₙ) − nx̄ = Σxᵢ − nx̄.
Since Σxᵢ = nx̄, this difference is nx̄ − nx̄ = 0.
Hence Σ(xᵢ − x̄) = 0.

items.stem: The mean of n observations is x̄, if the first term is increased by 1, second by 2 and so on. What will be the new mean ?
items.answer:
The first observation gains 1, the second gains 2, the third gains 3, and so on up to the nth observation, which gains n.
So the amount added to the total is 1 + 2 + 3 + … + n = n(n + 1)/2.
The new mean is the old mean plus this amount divided by n, that is x̄ + [n(n + 1)/2]/n.
Hence the new mean is x̄ + (n + 1)/2.

items.stem:
Traffic Management : A traffic enforcement camera is a camera which may be mounted beside or over a road or installed in an enforcement vehicle to detect motoring offenses, including speeding, vehicles going through a red traffic light. A worldwide review of studies found that speed cameras led to a reduction of 11% to 44% for fatal and serious injury crashes. The British Medical Journal recently reported that speed cameras were effective at reducing accidents and injuries in their vicinity and recommended wider deployment. In order to monitor reckless driving on Mumbai road, special cameras have been installed at many traffic light. The following table shows a frequency distribution table for the speed of 100 vehicles passing through a particular spot on a day.
Speed (in km/h)20-3030-4040-5050-6060-7070-8080-9090-100
Number of Vehicles13716352972
Based on the above information, answer the following questions. (i) Find the number of vehicles whose speed is more than 70 km/h ? (ii) Find the number of vehicles whose speed is less than 50 km/h ? (iii) What is the mode value of speed ? (iv) What is the median value of speed ? (v) Find the mean value of speed using empirical relation.
items.answer:
The cumulative frequencies are 1, 4, 11, 27, 62, 91, 98, 100, so N = 100.
(i) 62 vehicles have speed up to 70 km/h, so 100 − 62 = 38 vehicles have speed more than 70 km/h.
(ii) 11 vehicles have speed up to 50 km/h.
(iii) The maximum frequency is 35 for the class 60-70, so the modal class is 60-70 with l = 60, f₁ = 35, f₀ = 16, f₂ = 29 and h = 10. Mode = l + ((f₁ − f₀)/(2f₁ − f₀ − f₂))h = 60 + ((35 − 16)/(70 − 16 − 29)) × 10 = 60 + (19/25) × 10 = 60 + 7.6 = 67.6 km/h.
(iv) N/2 = 100/2 = 50; the first cumulative frequency greater than 50 is 62, so the median class is 60-70 with l = 60, F = 27, f = 35 and h = 10. Median = 60 + ((50 − 27)/35) × 10 = 60 + 6.57 = 66.57 km/h.
(v) By the empirical relation 3 Median = Mode + 2 Mean, so 3 × 66.57 = 67.6 + 2 Mean, giving 2 Mean = 199.71 − 67.6 = 132.11 and Mean = 66.06 km/h.
Hence 38 vehicles exceed 70 km/h, 11 are below 50 km/h, the mode is 67.6 km/h, the median is 66.57 km/h and the mean is about 66.06 km/h.

items.answer:
